title: Two dice: totals are not equally likely
familyTitle: Probability from the sample space of two dice or spinners
skill: Find the probability of a total with two dice/spinners by listing all m × n equally likely pairs.

knowledge: probability = favourable ÷ total for equally likely outcomes

concept: Each die gives each number equally often, so every PAIR (first, second) is equally likely: m × n pairs.
The totals are not equally likely: a middle total can be made by many pairs, an end total by only one.
explanation.visualNote: Reuses the table visual (the family's own method: 'Draw a table'); every cell is one equally likely pair.

workedExamples.prompt: Divya uses two spinners, each numbered 1 to 5. Each gives a number from 1 to 5, every number equally likely. What is the probability that the total of the two numbers is 8? (A fraction is fine.)
familyExplainSteps: 3 pairs fit: the total of the two numbers is 8

workedExamples.prompt: Anu uses a spinner numbered 1 to 4 and a spinner numbered 1 to 5. The first gives a number from 1 to 4 and the second a number from 1 to 5, every number equally likely. What is the probability that the total of the two numbers is 3? (A fraction is fine.)
familyExplainSteps: 2 pairs fit: the total of the two numbers is 3

alternativeExplanation.title: Why 7 is common with two dice
text: Total 2 needs (1,1): one way. Total 7 can be (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1): six ways.
Each way is equally likely, so 7 is six times as likely as 2.

misconceptions.status: modelled (a single matching answer is a SUSPECTED error; established only under misconception-evidence@1: two matching answers)
misconceptions.note: conceptual: outcomes (totals) taken as equally likely

whatWentWrong: In "Meena uses a spinner numbered 1 to 3 and a spinner numbered 1 to 5. The first gives a number from 1 to 3 and the second a number from 1 to 5, every number equally likely. What is the probability that the total of the two numbers is 6? (A fraction is fine.)", one wrong answer is 1/7.
The 7 possible totals were taken as equally likely. They are not: list all 15 pairs and count the ones that fit.
The pairs are equally likely, not the totals: count the pairs that give each total.
screens.counterCheck: Counter-check with two dice: total 2 is only (1,1), total 7 has six pairs; they cannot both be 1/11.

misconceptions.status: modelled (a single matching answer is a SUSPECTED error; established only under misconception-evidence@1: two matching answers)

whatWentWrong: In "Farhan uses two spinners, each numbered 1 to 3. Each gives a number from 1 to 3, every number equally likely. What is the probability that the total of the two numbers is 4? (A fraction is fine.)", one wrong answer is 2/9.
Pairs such as (1, 3) and (3, 1) were counted once. They are different outcomes: the first and second number are different.
(1,2) and (2,1) are different pairs: the first die and the second die are different objects.
screens.counterCheck: Counter-check: colour one die red: red 1 & blue 2 and red 2 & blue 1 are clearly two outcomes.

misconceptions.status: modelled (a single matching answer is a SUSPECTED error; established only under misconception-evidence@1: two matching answers)
misconceptions.note: procedural: sample space m + n instead of m × n

whatWentWrong: In "Lakshmi uses a spinner numbered 1 to 4 and a spinner numbered 1 to 5. The first gives a number from 1 to 4 and the second a number from 1 to 5, every number equally likely. What is the probability that the total of the two numbers is 2? (A fraction is fine.)", one wrong answer is 1/9.
The sample space was taken as 4 + 5 = 9 outcomes. Each of the 4 first numbers goes with each of the 5 second numbers: 4 × 5 = 20.
Each first number goes with EACH second number: m × n pairs, not m + n.
screens.counterCheck: Counter-check: two spinners numbered 1 to 3 give the pairs 11, 12, 13, 21, 22, 23, 31, 32, 33: 9 = 3 × 3 pairs, not 3 + 3 = 6.
